title: the-instance-address-is-resolved-never-spelled
owner: CC owns the sieve at build_inspector, the probe beside it, the conversions at the five callers, and the floor + charter edits at cairn/tools/base. Akien owns the two rulings this executes rather than proposes
intention: Make the instance address PHYSICS: a component that spells ~/.cairn by hand instead of asking cairn.tools.base.address is refused at the build inspection, and the seven standing hand-spellings go to zero first so the gate lands on a corpus it does not immediately red. Two halves, in that order. (a) CONVERT ALL SEVEN — four in aider_shim (driver.DEFAULT_DRIVES, fence.DEFAULT_RECORD, venv.VENV, probes/offload_yield_probe.ASK_LOG), ground_loop/discovery.instance_devices_root, and the two the probe called its permanent FLOOR: build_inspector/inspector.py:216 (resolve('instance/devices') has always been the device-across-instances shape, and the import allowlist that held it back was retired on 2026-08-12) and inference_domain/route.py:44 (ruled, and carrying a migration of live state — ~/.cairn/inference/hosts.json moves to ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/). (b) THE GATE — a new build_inspector sieve, one boolean per component, source-level and inference-free, composing the probe's existing scan rather than writing a second copy of the rule. Then the probe's floor drops to zero and base's charter loses the clause that says nothing refuses an eleventh spelling.
why: THE LIVED SYMPTOM: a resolver nobody is refused for ignoring is a convenience, and the corpus regrows the defect it was built to end. MEASURED, not predicted — on 2026-08-12 ten hand-spelled instance paths were converted down to two; on 2026-08-17 the armed probe measures SEVEN across 162 files and _enough() returns False. One new spelling per day for five days, four of them written by CC inside aider_shim, the device it was actively building, while the probe that names them sat armed and never fired. The cost is the one the resolver's own charter states: provisioning instance 1 of anything means finding and editing every copy, and a shipped app whose root is not under this developer's home directory cannot run at all. AND THE SHARPER WHY, which is about the disposition and not the paths: the probe's floor of two named both sites and both reasons, and both reasons had gone stale — one was answered by a function that predates the probe, the other by a ruling Akien made the same day, recorded two hundred lines away in the same component. A watch whose floor is never re-read goes on clearing against a world that moved.
traces_to: Law 4, by name and in its own words — 'a rule that matters is enforced by physics, not policy; until it is, it is a tracked debt (an IOU), not a resting state.' base's charter clause (8) states that debt verbatim ('nothing REFUSES an eleventh hand-spelled path... The enforcement is a tracked debt, not a resting state'), so this pays a declared IOU rather than opening a new rule. Law 1 — the resolver exists so a settled address is not re-derived; without a door the re-derivation continued, five times in five days. Law 9 — the red was measured and a deterministic red is fixed or carries a ruling, never a paragraph. Law 3 for the honesty of the close: the probe is the instrument, and the count must read zero by measurement, never by the floor being edited to match.

falsifier.proves_green: prove_gate: teeth beside the code at cairn/machines/build_inspector/proofs/ (the sieve), cairn/tools/base/proofs/ (the corpus reading) and cairn/devices/inference_domain/proofs/ (the migrated overlay read), each sealed by the tester under netns isolation and persisted through validation_store.persist_validation — the store's own door, never a hand-written trail (a live trouble is on file for that breach, and it recurred twice after being cleared, so it is named rather than assumed). check-type deterministic throughout: the sieve is inference-free by the inspector's own contract, and `cairn determinism` must still read the module PURE DETERMINISTIC after the addition. feedback_gate: a red routes to build_inspector for the sieve half and to cairn/tools/base for the resolver half — never to a converted caller, since every conversion is a mechanical substitution of one expression for an equal one.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when all four hold. (a) survey_class_space() reports ZERO sites on a scan that read more than zero files — the count and its denominator together, because a vacuous scan reports zero for the wrong reason. (b) _FLOOR_SITES is empty and _enough() returns True, read from the LIVE corpus and not from a fixture. (c) A PLANTED EIGHTH SPELLING REDS THE INSPECTION — the tooth a hollow build cannot pass, because a sieve that never fires is indistinguishable from no sieve, and after a successful conversion the corpus offers no live offender to demonstrate it on. (d) The two hardest conversions are proved at their own seams: route.py reads hosts.json from the new address, and the offload probe's ASK_LOG equals fence.DEFAULT_RECORD by Path equality rather than by two spellings agreeing. WRONG INTENT if the exemption set cannot be stated as a rule rather than a list of names — the scan must skip address.py, the watcher's own file and proofs/, all three sayable as 'a file whose job is to name or to assert the rule is not an instance of it'. A fourth exemption that cannot be said that way means the sieve has become the hand-widened allowlist that ticket reachability-replaces-the-allowlist retired at this same address, and the honest disposition is to route back to the AST shape.
falsifier.horizon: one build for the falsifier. The watch's horizon is the first component built after this that needs instance state — its author either reaches for instance_path or gets redded, and which one happens is the reading. That has a scheduled arrival rather than a hope: the queued inference-task log is itself a component about to need an instance address, and it is next in the sail batch.

children: none, and the reason is the finding itself. The conversion and the gate LOOK separately shippable — convert now, gate later — and that is exactly what was done on 2026-08-12, which produced seven sites five days later. Shipping the conversion alone is not a smaller version of this ticket; it is a re-run of an experiment whose result is already in hand. They are bound in the other direction too: the gate cannot land first without redding seven components at its first firing, a sweep the inspector's charter says should never be needed twice. One voyage under one falsifier, touching five components, no half of it provable alone.

questions.a: A DISPOSITIONED RED MUST RE-READ ITS DISPOSITION, OR IT IS JUST A RED WITH A STORY. The probe's floor named two sites and two reasons, and both reasons were stale: 'a device across instances, a shape none of the three rungs fits' when resolve('instance/devices') is that shape and predates the probe; 'its import allowlist is already red' when the allowlist was retired five days earlier by a ticket at that same address. The second site's disagreement had been RULED by Akien on 2026-08-12, and the ruling is recorded two hundred lines from the probe that calls it unsettled. Generalises: a floor is a recorded judgement about the world, and one with no re-read date is how a watch goes on clearing against a world that moved.

CONVERSION WITHOUT A DOOR IS A ONE-TIME CLEANUP, AND THIS IS THE MEASUREMENT RATHER THAN THE PREDICTION. Ten sites to two on 2026-08-12; seven on 2026-08-17. One new spelling per day, four written by CC inside the device it was actively building. The gate is not argued for from principle — the experiment already ran.

THE GATE AND THE WATCH ARE DIFFERENT INSTRUMENTS, AND THE FIVE-IN-FIVE-DAYS CASE PROVES IT. A sieve fires on the component being built and structurally cannot see a site in a component nobody is building — one of the five landed in ground_loop, which was not under build. The probe sweeps the whole corpus and carries no authority by construction (Law 6). The probe's floor going to zero is it reading a cleaner world, not it being retired.

THE ONE PLACE A HOLLOW GREEN HIDES, NAMED BEFORE THE BUILD: _FLOOR_SITES can be emptied without converting anything, and _enough() would then return True by moving the goalposts. So the falsifier demands two readings the wrong act cannot both satisfy — floor empty AND a live non-vacuous scan at zero — plus a planted eighth spelling, because a successful conversion leaves the gate with nothing live to prove itself on.

THE PROBE ASKED FOR THIS IMPORT AND COULD NOT HAVE IT. offload_yield_probe.py carries the comment 'Imported rather than re-spelled would be better, and is not possible without dragging the fence's whole import into a module the emission gate loads to READ'. address.py imports pathlib and nothing else — the leanness that was documented as a property is what makes it the answer to a request already written down in the corpus and left unanswered.

NOT IN SCOPE AND SAID SO: the AST-shaped rule (who may name the root at all), rejected for this build because Path.home() has legitimate non-.cairn uses on the very files being converted — venv.py's AIDER_SRC is a held foreign program — so an import-level rule would red a use the address module has no opinion about. Filed as an edge, not smuggled in. Also out and carried forward unchanged from the probe's own cast: the text rule cannot see a path built by concatenation from a variable or by a dynamic join.

THE SURVEY DEPOSIT REFUSED THREE HOURS AFTER THE SURVEY PASSED, AND THE TOLERANCE IT NEEDED WAS ALREADY BUILT — ON THE OTHER MOUTH. The survey berth's holding 15 is '/home/akien/.cairn/inference/hosts.json, 673 bytes, mtime 2026-08-08' — true when written at 18:11. The build then MOVED that overlay to the resolved four-rung address (devices/inference_domain/0/hosts.json) by Akien's 2026-08-12 ruling, which is the whole point of the voyage. At 21:0x the deposit refused: 'holding 15 names an address that does not resolve'. THE SHARP PART, and my first reading of it was wrong: the forwarding order IS consulted — inspector.survey_holdings_resolve, the PROMOTION-side sieve, filters its own findings through _resolves_to(address, ticket), and measured just now that call returns the successor for exactly this address off exactly this ticket's `forwarding` record. The pure judge_survey keeps the flat rule deliberately, and its docstring gives the reason: it is also the BERTH DOOR's mouth, and 'at berth time every holding resolves by definition', so 'only the promotion side, which alone stands downstream of a move, disposes'. THE DEFECT IS THAT THE DEPOSIT IS A THIRD MOUTH NOBODY COUNTED. deposit_survey calls validate_survey — the DOOR's gate — and a deposit stands downstream of a move exactly as promotion does. So the reasoning that justifies the flat rule is true of the berth and false of the deposit, and the deposit reuses the berth's mouth. A voyage that legitimately retires an address is therefore structurally unable to teach its own survey tree. Seven of eight berths deposited; survey is the one the trees did not get. Ticket owed.

A PROBE BERTHS WITH WHAT IT WATCHES, NOT WITH THE COMPONENT THAT OWNS THE TICKET. This ticket's component is cairn/tools/base; its watch sits at cairn/machines/build_inspector/probes/, because the thing being watched is the SIEVE REGISTRY and the registry is build_inspector's. The corpus half of the same question is read at cairn/tools/base/probes/hand_spelled_instance_paths.py, without authority. Two probes, two addresses, one question — and the split is not a duplication: a count alone cannot tell a working gate from a deleted one, so the half that reads the registry has to live where the registry is.

THE EXEMPTION COUNT WENT 3 -> 2 -> 3 WITHOUT ANYONE EDITING THE EXEMPTION SET, and that is the rule behaving correctly rather than drift. The cast predicted three exemptions; the AST shape retired one at PROVEME (2 over 274 files); at PROVED it reads 3 over 276 files because the corpus grew two files that legitimately bear weight. The set is CLOSED AT TWO DIALECTS — a rule, not a list of names — which is exactly the invariant test_address_rule.py pins, and the reason the count is allowed to move while the rule does not.

THE SEAL HAS TO BE CUT IN THE MOMENT BEFORE THE CLEARANCE, AND THIS COMPONENT PROVES WHY HARDER THAN ITS SIBLING. The clearance gate re-reads the seal's source fingerprint at the door; cairn/tools/base's fingerprint moves every time its own history.json is appended to — and the WATCHME crossing appends to it, immediately before the PROVED crossing that leans on the seal. A seal cut before the WATCHME would have had its horizon closed BY THE VOYAGE'S OWN BOOKKEEPING. Cut at 21:05:35, cleared minutes later, four checks clean.

A CHART'S SCORE IS NOT RECOVERABLE AS ONE NUMBER WHEN VOYAGES INTERLEAVE, AND THE HONEST REPORT SAYS SO. The rule is 'tool calls between the packet and done IS the packet's score, read downward'. This voyage's validate berth landed at 18:15 and its build closed at PROVEME; between PROVEME and this close, a second voyage (a-bulk-move-forwards-itself) and the askscan contamination fix both ran to completion in the same session. So the clean number is the BUILD window and the raw window is contaminated 3.7x — reported as both rather than as the flattering one.

watchme.trigger: read on demand, and materially after any build that adds instance state to a component. The population is the class-space corpus, which exists without arranging anything.
watchme.enough: DELIBERATELY ASYMMETRIC. ONE hand-spelled site standing in a component whose build ran the inspection after this ticket lands is STRONG falsification and satisfies it alone — it says the gate is present and did not bite, which is worse than no gate because a green gate is leaned on. THREE consecutive non-vacuous readings at zero, with at least one taken after a component that needed instance state was built, is WEAK confirmation and also satisfies it. A vacuous scan (files_scanned == 0) counts toward neither and is itself a red: a scan that read nothing reports zero, indistinguishable from a clean corpus at the moment the instrument has stopped working.
watchme.carrier: a verdict artifact against THIS ticket's falsifier, plus the probe's own readings: the site count, the files scanned, and — the half the sibling probe cannot report — whether the sieve is REGISTERED in build_inspector.SIEVES, since a rule deleted from the registry leaves the corpus clean and the gate absent, and those two facts read identically from a count alone.
watchme.nexus: cairn/machines/build_inspector — its how_it_learns surface, where the sieve registry is the thing being measured and probes/does_the_denied_set_stay_put.py already watches the neighbouring question of whether a denied set stays denied.
watchme.consumer: CC at the next build that needs instance state, and the resolver's own watch at cairn/tools/base/probes/hand_spelled_instance_paths.py, which reads the corpus half of the same question without authority.

Measured at cast rather than assumed: cairn.tools.base.address is already inside build_inspector/inspector.py's 26-file import closure (import_sieve.reaches), so the inspector's conversion adds no new reachability; and address.py imports pathlib and nothing else, which is what lets offload_yield_probe.py adopt it where it explicitly could NOT adopt fence.py — its own comment asked for exactly this and could not have it. ~/.cairn/inference/hosts.json exists on disk (673 bytes, mtime 2026-08-08) and ~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/ does not, so the route.py half carries a live-state migration, and address.py MAY NOT PROVISION — whoever creates that directory is not this module.

/home/akien/.cairn/inference/hosts.json.why: This build MOVED it, deliberately and by ruling: 'devices/inference_domain/0/ is exactly right. ruled with a smile' (Akien, 2026-08-12). The 673-byte overlay was copied byte-identical to the four-rung address and the old one removed, and route.OVERLAY_PATH now resolves through cairn.tools.base.address rather than spelling ~/.cairn by hand — which is the whole intention of this ticket. The survey berth survey-20260817T181131-7a8265794672.json holding 15 named the address as it stood at berth time (it was the thing being migrated, measured at 673 bytes, mtime 2026-08-08), so the chart falsified its own holding BY SUCCEEDING. That is precisely the case the forwarding order was built for on 2026-07-30 — a deliberate move a build makes on purpose — and it is a single hand-named address, not a bulk reorg (that class is ticket a-bulk-move-forwards-itself-from-gits-own-rename-record).

named_falsifications: SURVEY held a holding at an address THIS BUILD then retired by ruling — and the survey judge re-checks holdings at DEPOSIT time, so the packet that was true at write time could not teach its own tree. The claim falsified is not the holding; it is the judge's assumption that a holding's address is stable across the voyage it serves.

CONSTRAIN's bounds were written against a text-scan rule; the build changed the rule's SHAPE to an AST predicate over an expression, which retired one of the three exemptions the cast predicted. A bound stated over an implementation shape ages the moment the shape is the thing being changed.
DECOMPOSE.writes_to could not name the instance-space output this build produces (~/.cairn/devices/inference_domain/0/hosts.json) — n=2 for that narrowness across two voyages in one day.
SURVEY put inspector.py's registration site at :216; the sieve registered at :224.
VALIDATE criterion 1 names `files_scanned` where the producing vocabulary is `files_read` — the reader inventing the writer's key, the same shape as the aider_shim offload probe.
VALIDATE criterion 2 spells `_enough(now, {})`, which is the very signature the build measured as the defect and corrected to `_enough(context)`.
VALIDATE criteria 3 and 13 name `python3 -m pytest`; the proofs run as plain subprocesses under the tester and there is no pytest in the path.
VALIDATE criterion 9 names the pre-conversion site count (9) as the expected reading; the conversion ran inside the same voyage and the reading is 0.
HYPOTHESIZE counted the corpus per ADDRESS where the sieve attributes per deepest OWNER, so its expected count and the instrument's count were never the same quantity.
